# Context after the first observations, before the follow-up

The first 27 actual commands and all raw streams remain in observations-first/.
Three finite positive checks and deterministic distributions1/1/0 match the
independent predictions. Five deliberate finite negatives reach their intended
arity/category/condition boundaries. The duplication control and desired static
reuse instead stop earlier at the existing primitive-provider refusal: x is a
primitive, not an ordinary source fn provider. Neither result establishes the
later reusable-description or consumed-owner property. Two complete attempt-02
projects introduce an ordinary wrapped_x fn and replace only those provider names;
original first sources, predictions, diagnostics and hashes stay untouched.
This is an informed source repair after actual diagnostic feedback, not evidence
of model-independent repair success or a compiler feature change.

The first driver incorrectly constructed check --sized <project>. All ten JSON
and two text invocations returned actual usage errors before checking source.
That is a command-authoring mistake, not a source, semantic or compiler defect.
The actual help output and current src/bin/qleisli/sized.rs/source_plan adapter
confirm the supported sized check --entry=main::main --module=main=PATH form.
New explicitly authored commands will recheck unchanged attempt-01 sources
through that adapter. No command text is executed from the old observations.
The legacy sized adapter shares selected-source preparation/acceptance; agreement
with finite checks is a bounded public-interface observation, not two independent
implementations or a general cross-profile proof.

The pre-check follow-up inventory and predictions bind both new complete
projects before any subsequent CLI call. The fixed CLI/native hashes, explicit
QLEISLI_KERNEL environment, 0–2qubit bound and before/after identity checks remain.
No first source, corpus, library, examples, compiler or native executable changes.
